mental_model: An SA maps a customer problem to a few well-chosen services, then justifies the tradeoff against the Well-Architected pillars. Know each service in one line, plus when not to use it.
verify_note: Technical audit: October 15, 2026. Read the linked AWS sources in aws-terms.md for service guarantees and exceptions; verify model terms, Region support, quotas, and prices before the interview.

services.name: Region
services.one_liner: A geographic area with multiple isolated Availability Zones.
services.use_when: Choosing where to run: pick by latency to users, data residency rules, service availability, and price.
services.avoid_when: Do not spread across Regions by default; multi-Region adds cost and complexity, so do it only for DR, latency, or residency needs.

services.name: Availability Zone (AZ)
services.one_liner: One or more isolated data centers with independent power and networking inside a Region.
services.use_when: High availability: run across at least 2 AZs so one data center failing does not take you down.
services.avoid_when: Do not assume Multi-AZ protects against a full Region outage; that needs a multi-Region DR plan.

services.name: Edge location
services.one_liner: A CloudFront and Route 53 point of presence close to users.
services.use_when: Caching content and answering DNS near users to cut latency.
services.avoid_when: You cannot run general compute or databases there; it is for caching, DNS, and light edge functions.

services.name: Local Zones
services.one_liner: AWS compute and storage placed in a metro area, extending a Region.
services.use_when: Single-digit millisecond latency to users in one city: media rendering, gaming, real-time trading.
services.avoid_when: Most workloads; the parent Region is cheaper and has the full service set.

services.name: Wavelength
services.one_liner: AWS compute inside telecom 5G networks.
services.use_when: Ultra-low-latency apps for mobile devices on a carrier 5G network.
services.avoid_when: Users are not on a partner 5G network, or latency needs are ordinary.

services.name: Outposts
services.one_liner: AWS-managed hardware running in the customer's own data center.
services.use_when: Data must stay on premises, or the app needs very low latency to on-prem systems, but the team wants AWS APIs.
services.avoid_when: The workload can move to a Region; Outposts is a commitment with less elasticity.

services.name: EC2
services.one_liner: Virtual servers with full OS control.
services.use_when: Steady workloads, custom software, GPUs, or anything that needs OS-level control.
services.avoid_when: Spiky, event-driven, or short tasks where Lambda or Fargate removes server management.

services.name: Auto Scaling group
services.one_liner: Adds or removes EC2 instances by policy and replaces unhealthy ones.
services.use_when: Variable load and self-healing; target tracking on CPU or request count, scheduled scaling for known peaks.
services.avoid_when: Stateful single servers that cannot be replaced freely; move state out first.

services.name: Lambda
services.one_liner: Runs your code per event with no servers; up to 15 minutes per invocation.
services.use_when: Spiky, event-driven, short tasks: S3 uploads, API backends, queue consumers, glue code.
services.avoid_when: Long-running jobs over 15 minutes, steady very high throughput where containers are cheaper, GPU work, or strict cold-start budgets.

services.name: ECS
services.one_liner: AWS's own container orchestrator, simpler than Kubernetes.
services.use_when: Running containers without Kubernetes overhead, especially an AWS-only team.
services.avoid_when: The team already runs Kubernetes or needs portability across clouds; use EKS.

services.name: Fargate
services.one_liner: Serverless compute for ECS or EKS containers: no nodes to manage.
services.use_when: You want containers without patching or scaling hosts.
services.avoid_when: GPUs, daemon-style workloads, or large steady fleets where EC2 capacity is cheaper.

services.name: EKS
services.one_liner: Managed Kubernetes control plane.
services.use_when: The team already uses Kubernetes, wants portability, or needs its ecosystem (Helm, operators, Karpenter).
services.avoid_when: A small team new to Kubernetes; ECS or App Runner is less to operate.

services.name: Elastic Beanstalk
services.one_liner: Managed app platform: upload code, it provisions EC2, load balancer, and scaling.
services.use_when: Simple web apps that need a fast start with little infrastructure work.
services.avoid_when: Complex architectures that need fine control; use CloudFormation or CDK directly.

services.name: AWS Batch
services.one_liner: Managed queue and scheduler for batch compute jobs.
services.use_when: Large queued jobs: simulations, rendering, genomics, often on Spot.
services.avoid_when: Interactive or request-response workloads.

services.name: Graviton
services.one_liner: AWS-designed Arm processors for EC2, Lambda, RDS, and more.
services.use_when: Cutting cost per unit of work for code that runs on Arm, which most interpreted and JVM code does.
services.avoid_when: Software that only ships x86 binaries.

services.name: On-Demand pricing
services.one_liner: Pay by the second or hour with no commitment.
services.use_when: New or unpredictable workloads and short experiments.
services.avoid_when: Steady baseline load; Savings Plans are much cheaper for it.

services.name: Savings Plans and Reserved Instances
services.one_liner: A 1 or 3 year commitment in exchange for a large discount.
services.use_when: The steady baseline you know you will run.
services.avoid_when: Workloads you might shut down or move soon.

services.name: Spot Instances
services.one_liner: Spare EC2 capacity at a deep discount that AWS can reclaim with a 2-minute warning.
services.use_when: Fault-tolerant, interruptible work: batch, CI, stateless web tiers mixed with On-Demand, ML training with checkpoints.
services.avoid_when: Databases or anything that cannot handle sudden interruption.

services.name: S3
services.one_liner: Object storage designed for 11 nines of durability; versioning, replication, lifecycle rules.
services.use_when: Data lakes, backups, static assets, ML datasets, logs; anything accessed as whole objects.
services.avoid_when: Low-latency block storage for a database or a POSIX file system; use EBS or EFS.

services.name: S3 storage classes
services.one_liner: Standard, Intelligent-Tiering, Standard-IA, One Zone-IA, Glacier Instant, Flexible, and Deep Archive.
services.use_when: Matching cost to access pattern; lifecycle rules move objects down as they cool.
services.avoid_when: Infrequent-access classes for small or short-lived objects: minimum size and duration charges can cost more.

services.name: S3 Intelligent-Tiering
services.one_liner: Moves objects between access tiers automatically based on use.
services.use_when: Access patterns are unknown or change over time.
services.avoid_when: Access is predictable; a plain lifecycle rule avoids the monitoring fee.

services.name: EBS
services.one_liner: Block storage volumes for one EC2 instance in one AZ (gp3, io2); snapshots go to S3.
services.use_when: Boot volumes and databases on EC2 that need low-latency block storage.
services.avoid_when: Sharing a file system across many instances (use EFS) or storing large object data (use S3).

services.name: EFS
services.one_liner: Managed shared NFS file system across many instances and AZs.
services.use_when: Shared files for Linux fleets, containers, or lift-and-shift apps that expect a file system.
services.avoid_when: Windows file shares (FSx for Windows) or cheap bulk storage (S3).

services.name: FSx
services.one_liner: Managed third-party file systems: Windows File Server, Lustre, NetApp ONTAP, OpenZFS.
services.use_when: Windows SMB shares, HPC scratch with Lustre, or migrating NetApp workloads unchanged.
services.avoid_when: Plain Linux shared storage; EFS is simpler.

services.name: Storage Gateway
services.one_liner: Hybrid storage that presents cloud storage to on-prem apps as file, volume, or tape.
services.use_when: On-prem apps need to keep working while data moves to S3, or tape backup moves to the cloud.
services.avoid_when: One-time data transfer; assess DataSync or supported offline options rather than adding a persistent gateway.

services.name: Snowball
services.one_liner: Physical offline data-transfer devices; availability and customer eligibility must be checked.
services.use_when: Existing eligible customers with a supported offline transfer need; confirm current ordering eligibility before recommending.
services.avoid_when: Assuming new customers can order Snowball; compare DataSync, Direct Connect, and transfer partners for current alternatives.

services.name: DataSync
services.one_liner: Online transfer service that moves and syncs files between on-prem and AWS storage.
services.use_when: Network migration of file data to S3, EFS, or FSx, with scheduling and verification.
services.avoid_when: Database migration (use DMS) or bulk data over a constrained link; compare dedicated connectivity and currently eligible offline-transfer options.

services.name: RDS
services.one_liner: Managed relational databases with backups, patching, and failover options.
services.use_when: Joins and transactions. Multi-AZ DB instance: synchronous non-readable standby for HA. Multi-AZ DB cluster (supported MySQL/PostgreSQL versions): writer plus two readable standbys across three AZs. Read replicas generally replicate asynchronously for read scaling.
services.avoid_when: Massive key-value scale with simple access patterns (DynamoDB) or analytics over huge datasets (Redshift).

services.name: Aurora
services.one_liner: AWS-built MySQL and PostgreSQL-compatible database with storage replicated across 3 AZs, up to 15 read replicas, a Serverless option, and Global Database.
services.use_when: High-performance relational workloads, fast failover, or cross-Region reads and DR.
services.avoid_when: Small, cheap, steady databases where standard RDS costs less.

services.name: DynamoDB
services.one_liner: Serverless key-value and document database with single-digit millisecond reads at any scale; DAX cache, Streams, global tables.
services.use_when: Known access patterns at high scale: sessions, carts, user profiles, IoT, leaderboards.
services.avoid_when: Ad hoc queries, many-table joins, or analytics; and design the partition key carefully to avoid hot partitions.

services.name: ElastiCache
services.one_liner: Managed in-memory cache: Redis OSS, Valkey, Memcached.
services.use_when: Caching hot reads, sessions, leaderboards, rate limiting.
services.avoid_when: As the only copy of durable data; use MemoryDB if you need durability with Redis APIs.

services.name: MemoryDB
services.one_liner: Durable, Redis-compatible in-memory database with a multi-AZ transaction log.
services.use_when: Microsecond reads where the in-memory store is the primary database.
services.avoid_when: A cache in front of another database; ElastiCache is cheaper.

services.name: Redshift
services.one_liner: Columnar data warehouse for SQL analytics at scale; Serverless option.
services.use_when: BI and reporting over large structured datasets with complex joins.
services.avoid_when: Transactional workloads or occasional queries on S3 data; Athena may be cheaper.

services.name: DocumentDB
services.one_liner: Managed document database with MongoDB API compatibility.
services.use_when: Moving MongoDB workloads to a managed service.
services.avoid_when: Simple key-value at massive scale (DynamoDB) or relational needs (RDS).

services.name: Neptune
services.one_liner: Managed graph database (property graph and RDF).
services.use_when: Highly connected data: fraud rings, recommendations, knowledge graphs. Ties to your GNN fraud project.
services.avoid_when: Data that is not relationship-heavy; a relational or key-value store is simpler.

services.name: Timestream
services.one_liner: Managed time-series database.
services.use_when: IoT telemetry, metrics, and events queried by time windows.
services.avoid_when: General transactional data.

services.name: OpenSearch Service
services.one_liner: Managed search and log analytics; also a vector store for RAG.
services.use_when: Full-text search, log analytics dashboards, vector search for retrieval.
services.avoid_when: As the system of record; keep the source of truth in a database or S3.

services.name: Database Migration Service (DMS)
services.one_liner: Migrates databases to AWS with ongoing change data capture to keep source and target in sync.
services.use_when: Moving a database with minimal downtime; pair with Schema Conversion for engine changes.
services.avoid_when: File or object data (use DataSync).

services.name: VPC
services.one_liner: Your private, isolated network in a Region, with subnets per AZ.
services.use_when: Control networking for resources such as EC2, RDS, and internal load balancers. S3 and DynamoDB are regional managed services accessed through APIs; a customer VPC is not required for every design.
services.avoid_when: Adding VPC attachment to Lambda without a private-resource requirement; plan non-overlapping CIDRs and endpoint/egress paths when a VPC is needed.

services.name: Public and private subnets
services.one_liner: A subnet is public if its route table points to an Internet Gateway, private otherwise.
services.use_when: Load balancers in public subnets; app servers and databases in private ones.
services.avoid_when: Putting databases or app servers in public subnets.

services.name: Internet Gateway
services.one_liner: Lets resources in public subnets reach and be reached from the internet.
services.use_when: Any VPC that serves public traffic.
services.avoid_when: Private-only workloads; use VPC endpoints and NAT instead.

services.name: NAT Gateway
services.one_liner: Lets private subnets make outbound internet connections without accepting inbound ones.
services.use_when: Private instances need patches or external APIs.
services.avoid_when: Heavy traffic to S3 or DynamoDB; gateway endpoints are free and skip NAT data charges.

services.name: Security group
services.one_liner: Stateful virtual firewall on an instance or network interface; allow rules only.
services.use_when: Default access control: reference other security groups instead of IP ranges.
services.avoid_when: You need an explicit deny for a subnet; that is a NACL.

services.name: Network ACL
services.one_liner: Stateless subnet-level firewall with ordered allow and deny rules.
services.use_when: Blocking a known bad IP range for a whole subnet, as a second layer.
services.avoid_when: As the main control; being stateless, you must allow return traffic explicitly.

services.name: VPC peering
services.one_liner: A private one-to-one connection between two VPCs; not transitive.
services.use_when: Connecting a few VPCs simply.
services.avoid_when: Many VPCs or on-prem links; use Transit Gateway as a hub.

services.name: Transit Gateway
services.one_liner: A regional hub that connects many VPCs and on-prem networks.
services.use_when: Dozens of VPCs and accounts, plus VPN or Direct Connect.
services.avoid_when: Two VPCs; peering is cheaper.

services.name: PrivateLink and VPC endpoints
services.one_liner: Private access to AWS services or partner services without the internet; gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB.
services.use_when: Compliance requires traffic to stay off the internet, or to cut NAT costs.
services.avoid_when: Services already reachable privately another way.

services.name: Direct Connect
services.one_liner: A dedicated private line from your data center to AWS.
services.use_when: Consistent bandwidth and latency for hybrid workloads or large ongoing transfers.
services.avoid_when: You need it next week; provisioning takes time. Start with Site-to-Site VPN.

services.name: Site-to-Site VPN
services.one_liner: An encrypted tunnel over the internet between on-prem and a VPC.
services.use_when: Fast, cheap hybrid connectivity, or as backup for Direct Connect.
services.avoid_when: You need guaranteed bandwidth and latency.

services.name: Application Load Balancer
services.one_liner: Layer 7 load balancer: routes HTTP and HTTPS by path, host, and header.
services.use_when: Web apps and microservices, containers, path-based routing, TLS termination.
services.avoid_when: Non-HTTP protocols, static IPs, or extreme throughput; use NLB.

services.name: Network Load Balancer
services.one_liner: Layer 4 load balancer for TCP, UDP, and TLS with static IPs and very low latency.
services.use_when: Very high throughput, non-HTTP protocols, static IPs for allow-lists, PrivateLink services.
services.avoid_when: You need HTTP routing rules; use ALB.

services.name: Gateway Load Balancer
services.one_liner: Distributes traffic to third-party network appliances such as firewalls.
services.use_when: Inserting inspection appliances transparently into traffic flows.
services.avoid_when: Ordinary app load balancing.

services.name: Route 53
services.one_liner: DNS with health checks and routing policies: simple, weighted, latency, failover, geolocation, geoproximity, multivalue.
services.use_when: Domain names, failover between Regions, weighted canary releases, latency-based routing.
services.avoid_when: Expecting instant failover; clients cache DNS for the TTL.

services.name: CloudFront
services.one_liner: CDN delivering static and dynamic HTTP content through edge locations.
services.use_when: Global web delivery, origin offload, WAF, and TLS at the edge; uncacheable dynamic requests can benefit from edge connections and the AWS network. Disable caching for sensitive personalized paths.
services.avoid_when: Non-HTTP protocols or a measured workload where added edge delivery gives no benefit; compare Global Accelerator for static IPs and regional routing.

services.name: Global Accelerator
services.one_liner: Static anycast IPs that route users over the AWS backbone to the nearest healthy endpoint.
services.use_when: Non-HTTP or latency-sensitive global apps needing fast regional failover and fixed IPs.
services.avoid_when: Cacheable web content; CloudFront fits better.

services.name: API Gateway
services.one_liner: Managed REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs with auth, throttling, and usage plans.
services.use_when: A front door for Lambda or microservices with auth and rate limits.
services.avoid_when: Very high, steady traffic to containers where an ALB is cheaper.

services.name: IAM
services.one_liner: Users, groups, roles, and JSON policies that decide who can do what.
services.use_when: Every access decision; follow least privilege.
services.avoid_when: Long-lived access keys for humans; use roles and Identity Center.

services.name: IAM role
services.one_liner: An identity that is assumed and gives temporary credentials.
services.use_when: Apps on EC2, Lambda, and containers, cross-account access, and federated humans.
services.avoid_when: Never embed access keys in code instead of using a role.

services.name: Organizations and SCPs
services.one_liner: Groups accounts; service control policies set guardrails no account can exceed.
services.use_when: Multi-account setups: separate prod, dev, security, and billing.
services.avoid_when: SCPs do not grant permissions; they only limit them.

services.name: IAM Identity Center
services.one_liner: Single sign-on for people across AWS accounts and apps.
services.use_when: Workforce access to many accounts, federated with an existing identity provider.
services.avoid_when: Customer sign-in for your app; that is Cognito.

services.name: KMS
services.one_liner: Managed encryption keys; every key use is logged in CloudTrail.
services.use_when: Encryption at rest for S3, EBS, RDS, and app data, with key policies controlling use.
services.avoid_when: Storing secrets like passwords; use Secrets Manager.

services.name: Secrets Manager
services.one_liner: Stores secrets with automatic rotation.
services.use_when: Database passwords and API keys that should rotate.
services.avoid_when: Plain config values; Parameter Store is cheaper.

services.name: Systems Manager Parameter Store
services.one_liner: Hierarchical storage for config and simple secrets.
services.use_when: App config and feature flags; low-cost secure strings.
services.avoid_when: Secrets that need built-in rotation.

services.name: Certificate Manager (ACM)
services.one_liner: Manages TLS certificates; integrated non-exportable public certificates have no certificate charge.
services.use_when: HTTPS on supported AWS integrations; exportable public certificates can support servers outside those integrations, with charges.
services.avoid_when: Assuming all certificates are free or cannot be exported; check certificate type, integration support, and renewal deployment.

services.name: WAF
services.one_liner: Layer 7 web firewall rules: SQL injection, XSS, rate limits, bot control.
services.use_when: In front of CloudFront, ALB, or API Gateway for public apps.
services.avoid_when: Network-level DDoS alone; Shield covers that layer.

services.name: Shield
services.one_liner: DDoS protection; Standard is automatic and free, Advanced adds response team and cost protection.
services.use_when: Advanced for high-profile public apps that cannot go down.
services.avoid_when: Paying for Advanced on small internal apps.

services.name: GuardDuty
services.one_liner: Threat detection from CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and DNS logs.
services.use_when: Turn it on in every account to catch compromised credentials and odd behavior.
services.avoid_when: Expecting it to block anything; it detects, other tools respond.

services.name: Inspector
services.one_liner: Scans EC2, container images, and Lambda for vulnerabilities.
services.use_when: Continuous vulnerability management.
services.avoid_when: Runtime threat detection; that is GuardDuty.

services.name: Macie
services.one_liner: Finds sensitive data such as PII in S3.
services.use_when: Compliance audits of data lakes and buckets.
services.avoid_when: Data that is not in S3.

services.name: Security Hub
services.one_liner: Aggregates security findings and checks against standards across accounts.
services.use_when: One view of security posture in a multi-account setup.
services.avoid_when: Single small accounts with little to aggregate.

services.name: CloudTrail
services.one_liner: Records who made which API call, when, and from where.
services.use_when: Auditing, forensics, and compliance; send it to a locked central bucket.
services.avoid_when: Performance metrics; that is CloudWatch.

services.name: AWS Config
services.one_liner: Tracks resource configuration over time and checks it against rules.
services.use_when: Proving compliance and catching drift, like an open security group.
services.avoid_when: Tracking API calls; that is CloudTrail.

services.name: Cognito
services.one_liner: User sign-up, sign-in, and tokens for your own apps.
services.use_when: Customer-facing login, social sign-in, and securing APIs with JWTs.
services.avoid_when: Workforce SSO into AWS accounts; use Identity Center.

services.name: SQS
services.one_liner: Managed queue: Standard has at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering; FIFO orders within each message group and deduplicates sends within a 5-minute window.
services.use_when: Buffering spikes and retries with a DLQ. Use idempotent consumers: a crash after a side effect but before deletion can cause processing again, even with FIFO.
services.avoid_when: Treating FIFO deduplication as end-to-end exactly-once side effects; use SNS fan-out for independent subscribers or Kinesis for replayable streams.

services.name: SNS
services.one_liner: Pub/sub push to many subscribers.
services.use_when: Fan-out: one event to many SQS queues, Lambdas, emails, or SMS.
services.avoid_when: Durable buffering for a slow consumer; put SQS behind it.

services.name: EventBridge
services.one_liner: Serverless event bus with content-based routing rules, SaaS and AWS events, and schedules.
services.use_when: Event-driven architectures across services, reacting to AWS events, cron jobs.
services.avoid_when: High-throughput ordered streams; use Kinesis or MSK.

services.name: Step Functions
services.one_liner: Workflow orchestration with state, retries, branching, and human-approval waits.
services.use_when: Multi-step processes like agent pipelines, document processing, order flows. Fits your S1 story.
services.avoid_when: One simple step; a single Lambda is enough.

services.name: Kinesis Data Streams
services.one_liner: Real-time ordered streams by shard that many consumers can replay.
services.use_when: Clickstreams, telemetry, real-time analytics with multiple consumers.
services.avoid_when: Simple job queues; SQS is cheaper and simpler.

services.name: Data Firehose
services.one_liner: Loads streaming data into S3, Redshift, OpenSearch, and others with buffering and transforms.
services.use_when: Getting streams into storage with no consumer code.
services.avoid_when: Sub-second processing or custom consumers; use Kinesis Data Streams.

services.name: MSK
services.one_liner: Managed Apache Kafka.
services.use_when: Teams already on Kafka, or needing its ecosystem and semantics.
services.avoid_when: New simple streaming needs; Kinesis has less to operate.

services.name: Glue
services.one_liner: Serverless Spark ETL plus the Glue Data Catalog of table metadata.
services.use_when: ETL into a data lake and a shared catalog for Athena, EMR, and Redshift.
services.avoid_when: Long-running heavily tuned Spark clusters; EMR gives more control.

services.name: Athena
services.one_liner: Serverless SQL directly on data in S3; pay per data scanned.
services.use_when: Ad hoc queries on a data lake; partition and use columnar formats to cut cost.
services.avoid_when: Heavy, constant BI workloads; Redshift is cheaper at that volume.

services.name: Lake Formation
services.one_liner: Fine-grained permissions on data lake tables, columns, and rows.
services.use_when: Many teams share one data lake with different access rights.
services.avoid_when: A single team and a few buckets.

services.name: EMR
services.one_liner: Managed Spark, Hadoop, and Presto clusters, on EC2, EKS, or Serverless.
services.use_when: Large or tuned Spark jobs; migrating existing Hadoop. Maps to your Databricks work.
services.avoid_when: Small ETL that Glue handles without clusters.

services.name: QuickSight
services.one_liner: Managed BI dashboards, with natural-language Q and A.
services.use_when: Dashboards for business users on top of Athena, Redshift, or RDS.
services.avoid_when: The customer has standardized on another BI tool.

services.name: Amazon Bedrock
services.one_liner: Managed API to foundation models (Anthropic Claude, Amazon Nova, Llama, and others).
services.use_when: Generative AI without managing model infrastructure. Verify the selected model and API retention terms, invocation logging, and inference routing before promising privacy or residency.
services.avoid_when: A custom model architecture requires training or hosting control; consider SageMaker AI. Cross-Region inference can process data beyond the source Region.

services.name: Bedrock Knowledge Bases
services.one_liner: Managed RAG: ingests documents, chunks and embeds them into a vector store, retrieves at query time.
services.use_when: Answering questions over company documents with citations.
services.avoid_when: Answers depend on live transactional data better fetched by a tool call.

services.name: Bedrock Agents
services.one_liner: Agents that plan and call your APIs through action groups, often backed by Lambda.
services.use_when: Multi-step tasks that need tools: the AWS-native version of your MCP connectors.
services.avoid_when: A fixed workflow; Step Functions is more predictable.

services.name: Bedrock Guardrails
services.one_liner: Filters for harmful content, denied topics, PII, and grounding checks on model input and output.
services.use_when: Any customer-facing GenAI app, especially in regulated industries.
services.avoid_when: Using content filters as authorization or access control. Guardrails do not replace IAM, document permissions, trusted retrieval filters, evaluations, or monitoring.

services.name: SageMaker AI
services.one_liner: Build, train, tune, and deploy your own models; real-time, serverless, async, and batch endpoints.
services.use_when: Custom models, fine-tuning, or full control of ML pipelines.
services.avoid_when: Calling an existing foundation model is enough; Bedrock is faster to ship.

services.name: Amazon Q
services.one_liner: Generative AI assistants: Q Business over company data, Q Developer for coding and AWS help.
services.use_when: Customers want an assistant without building one.
services.avoid_when: They need a custom app experience; build on Bedrock.

services.name: Trainium
services.one_liner: AWS-built chips for training models at lower cost (Trn instances).
services.use_when: Large training jobs where cost per run matters.
services.avoid_when: Code tied to CUDA-only libraries without porting effort.

services.name: Inferentia
services.one_liner: AWS-built chips for low-cost, high-throughput inference (Inf instances).
services.use_when: High-volume inference where cost per token or prediction dominates.
services.avoid_when: Small or bursty inference; serverless or Bedrock may be cheaper.

services.name: Rekognition
services.one_liner: Image and video analysis: labels, faces, text, moderation.
services.use_when: Vision features without training a model.
services.avoid_when: Highly custom visual tasks; train with SageMaker AI.

services.name: Textract
services.one_liner: Extracts text, forms, and tables from documents.
services.use_when: Invoices, forms, and scanned documents into structured data.
services.avoid_when: Clean digital text that needs no OCR.

services.name: Comprehend
services.one_liner: NLP service: entities, sentiment, key phrases, PII detection, classification.
services.use_when: Standard text analytics at scale without an LLM.
services.avoid_when: Open-ended generation or reasoning; use Bedrock.

services.name: Transcribe
services.one_liner: Speech to text.
services.use_when: Call center transcripts, captions, voice notes.
services.avoid_when: Text input already exists.

services.name: Polly
services.one_liner: Text to speech.
services.use_when: Voice output for apps, IVR, accessibility.
services.avoid_when: No audio output is needed.

services.name: Translate
services.one_liner: Neural machine translation.
services.use_when: Localizing content and support at scale.
services.avoid_when: Legal or brand copy that needs human review anyway.

services.name: Kendra
services.one_liner: Managed enterprise search with connectors to many document sources.
services.use_when: Search across company repositories with access controls.
services.avoid_when: A simple RAG app; Bedrock Knowledge Bases may be enough.

services.name: Augmented AI (A2I)
services.one_liner: Routes low-confidence ML predictions to human reviewers.
services.use_when: Human-in-the-loop review, like your S1 and S10 stories.
services.avoid_when: Predictions that are always confident or always reviewed.

services.name: CloudWatch
services.one_liner: Metrics, logs, alarms, and dashboards; Application Signals adds SLOs.
services.use_when: Monitoring and alerting on everything you run.
services.avoid_when: Auditing API calls (CloudTrail) or configuration history (Config).

services.name: X-Ray
services.one_liner: Distributed tracing across services.
services.use_when: Finding which service in a chain is slow or failing.
services.avoid_when: A single monolith where logs and metrics are enough.

services.name: Managed Service for Prometheus
services.one_liner: Managed, Prometheus-compatible metrics storage and querying.
services.use_when: Kubernetes and teams already on Prometheus. Maps to your Oracle work.
services.avoid_when: Teams fine with CloudWatch metrics alone.

services.name: Managed Grafana
services.one_liner: Managed Grafana dashboards over Prometheus, CloudWatch, and other sources.
services.use_when: Teams that already use Grafana dashboards.
services.avoid_when: CloudWatch dashboards already cover the need.

services.name: CloudFormation
services.one_liner: Infrastructure as code in YAML or JSON templates.
services.use_when: Repeatable, reviewable environments; drift detection.
services.avoid_when: Clicking in the console for anything that will live long.

services.name: CDK
services.one_liner: Infrastructure as code in real programming languages that synthesizes CloudFormation.
services.use_when: Developer teams who want loops, types, and reusable constructs.
services.avoid_when: Teams standardized on Terraform.

services.name: CodePipeline and CodeBuild
services.one_liner: Managed CI/CD pipelines and build runners.
services.use_when: AWS-native CI/CD with validation stages. Maps to your Jenkins toolchain.
services.avoid_when: The team already runs GitHub Actions well; connect it to AWS with OIDC roles.

services.name: Systems Manager
services.one_liner: Patching, run commands, Session Manager shell access, Automation runbooks.
services.use_when: Operating fleets without SSH keys or bastion hosts.
services.avoid_when: Fully serverless stacks with no instances.

services.name: Trusted Advisor
services.one_liner: Checks for cost, security, fault tolerance, performance, and service limits.
services.use_when: Quick best-practice review of an account.
services.avoid_when: Deep architecture review; run a Well-Architected review.

services.name: Cost Explorer
services.one_liner: Visualizes and forecasts spend by service, account, and tag.
services.use_when: Finding what drives the bill; requires good cost allocation tags.
services.avoid_when: Alerting on overspend; that is Budgets.

services.name: Budgets
services.one_liner: Alerts and actions when cost or usage crosses a threshold.
services.use_when: Every account, so surprises surface early.
services.avoid_when: Treating an alert or automated budget action as a guaranteed spending cap; billing updates and actions can lag.

services.name: Compute Optimizer
services.one_liner: Right-sizing recommendations for EC2, EBS, Lambda, and more from real usage.
services.use_when: Cutting over-provisioned resources.
services.avoid_when: Workloads with too little history to judge.

services.name: Control Tower
services.one_liner: Sets up a governed multi-account landing zone with guardrails.
services.use_when: A new enterprise or migration needs accounts, logging, and guardrails from day one.
services.avoid_when: A single-account prototype.

pillars.name: Operational Excellence
pillars.question: How do you run, monitor, and improve the workload?
pillars.tie: Your P1 MTTR and CLI toolchain stories.

pillars.name: Security
pillars.question: How do you protect data, systems, and identities?
practices: Encrypt at rest and in transit
pillars.tie: Field-level audit trail in the ERP migration.

pillars.name: Reliability
pillars.question: How does it recover from failure and meet demand?
pillars.tie: p99 SLOs held at 2x peak load.

pillars.name: Performance Efficiency
pillars.question: How do you use resources efficiently as demand changes?
practices: Use managed and serverless where it fits

pillars.name: Cost Optimization
pillars.question: How do you deliver value at the lowest price?
practices: Right-size, then commit with Savings Plans

pillars.name: Sustainability
pillars.question: How do you minimize environmental impact?
practices: Delete data you do not need
pillars.tie: Fewer false pages, fewer wasted cycles.

seven_rs.name: Retire
seven_rs.what: Turn it off; nobody needs it.
seven_rs.example: An old reporting server no one has opened in a year.

seven_rs.name: Retain
seven_rs.what: Keep it where it is for now.
seven_rs.example: A system with a hardware dependency or a recent upgrade.

seven_rs.name: Rehost (lift and shift)
seven_rs.example: A VM fleet moved with Application Migration Service to hit a data center exit date.

seven_rs.name: Relocate
seven_rs.what: Move the hypervisor-level platform without changing apps.
seven_rs.example: VMware workloads moved to VMware on AWS.

seven_rs.name: Repurchase
seven_rs.example: Your ERP story: Sage X3 to Sage Intacct, with a data migration.

seven_rs.name: Replatform (lift and reshape)
seven_rs.what: A few cloud optimizations without changing core architecture.

seven_rs.name: Refactor (re-architect)
seven_rs.example: A monolith split into services on Lambda and DynamoDB.

dr_tiers.name: Backup and restore
dr_tiers.how: Back up to S3 or AWS Backup in another Region; rebuild infrastructure with IaC when needed.

dr_tiers.name: Pilot light
dr_tiers.how: Data replicates continuously; core services are off or minimal until a failover scales them up.

dr_tiers.name: Warm standby
dr_tiers.how: A scaled-down full copy runs in the second Region and scales up on failover.

dr_tiers.name: Multi-site active/active
dr_tiers.how: Both Regions serve traffic; consistency and conflict handling determine write safety. Aurora Global Database is single-writer across Regions, even with write forwarding. All tier timings are illustrative targets, not guarantees; test end-to-end recovery.

dr_terms.meaning: Recovery point objective: how much data loss, measured in time, the business accepts.
Recovery time objective: how long the business accepts being down.

customer: OS and app patching on EC2
shared_responsibility.note: The line moves up as services get more managed: on Lambda and DynamoDB, AWS handles the OS and runtime.

other_frameworks.name: Working Backwards (PR-FAQ)
other_frameworks.what: Start from the customer: write the press release and FAQ before building.

other_frameworks.name: Cloud Adoption Framework (CAF)
other_frameworks.what: Six perspectives for a cloud program: business, people, governance, platform, security, operations.
